sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Lightweight Ad-Monetized Mobile Games

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (national single-jurisdiction regime; no sub-state tax distinctions)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic; codified commercial code and company statutes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: U.S.-Colombia Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 15 May 2012; Investment Chapter with investor-state arbitration)
Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement (in force 15 August 2011; Chapter 8 on Investment)
United Kingdom-Colombia Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 1 January 2015)
Colombia-South Korea Free Trade Agreement (in force 15 July 2016; investment provisions)
European Union-Colombia-Peru-Ecuador Trade Agreement (provisionally applicable since 1 August 2013)
Pacific Alliance Framework Agreement (Alianza del Pacifico; investment facilitation platform)
DTAAs in force: Spain, France, United Kingdom, Mexico, South Korea and Portugal (plus protocol with Chile)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (UIAF), Ley 1121 de 2006 (terrorist financing), Ley 1762 de 2015 (AML/CFT aggravations); Codigo de Comercio Libro II; Decreto 1068 de 2015 (financial sector recast); Circular Externa 029 de 2017 of the Superintendencia Financiera (SARLAFT); Decreto 1670 de 2021 (beneficiario final declaration in the RUES corporate registry, as amended); Estatuto Tributario Art. 631-5 (beneficial-owner information transmitted to DIAN, added by Ley 2010 de 2019); alignment with FATF Recommendations 10, 24 and 25.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access - beneficial owner data filed with the Camaras de Comercio/RUES, DIAN and UIAF; no publicly searchable register comparable to the United Kingdom PSC regime; access by judicial, fiscal and FIUs on legitimate request.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Poder Especial (special power of attorney) granted by each foreign shareholder to the local incorporator and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: U.S. Notary Public, County Clerk and Secretary of State (or equivalent competent authority in the shareholder's country of origin)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention in force for Colombia since January 2001; implementing statute Ley 455 de 1998)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence and Good Standing of each foreign corporate shareholder (when the shareholder is a legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-jurisdiction companies registrar (e.g., Delaware or Colorado Secretary of State)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille followed by official Spanish sworn translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (or corporate extracts evidencing the signatory's authority) of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille followed by official Spanish sworn translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified passport copy and residential proof of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: U.S. Notary Public (or authorized apostille-issuing authority in the UBO's country of residence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification; apostille only where the Chamber of Commerce requires legalization of identity documents for foreign UBOs

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives and UBOs against (i) the OFAC SDN list, (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, (iv) Colombian UIAF risk and PEP lists, and (v) domestic 'lista de riesgo' databases maintained by the Camaras de Comercio and SIC; PEP status is documented in the SARLAFT-oriented KYC file; adverse-media and source-of-funds checks accompany the beneficial-ownership proof pack and must be refreshed within 90 days of incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES - Registro Unico Empresarial y Social (https://www.rue.com.co) administered by Confecamaras and operated by the local Camara de Comercio (e.g., Camara de Comercio de Bogota online homonymy and name-reservation module)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company denomination must be expressed in Spanish (or romanized Latin script); names must terminate with 'S.A.S.' or 'Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada'; foreign-script characters (Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic) are not accepted; a fantasy denomination may combine words, numbers and recognized Latin letters provided it is not identical to, or confusingly similar with, any registered enterprise used in the same economic sector.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RUES/Chamber rejects the proposed name for homonymy, prohibited terms or deceptive similarity, the incorporator may within 10 working days: (1) file a reconsideration petition (recurso de reposicion) before the same Camara de Comercio, (2) attach a fresh homonymy certificate and a legal memorandum distinguishing the marks, (3) request the supplementary appeal (recurso de apelacion) to the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio - SIC where the Chamber denies relief, and (4) alternatively re-file under a new denomination immediately; the reserved name lapses after 30 calendar days unless the incorporation filing is completed, in which case reservation extension of another 30 days may be requested through the chamber portal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. The S.A.S. must designate a real domicile address within the municipality of the registered seat (Law 1258 de 2008 and Codigo de Comercio Art. 110), with a legal process-agent capable of receiving judicial notices; P.O.-Box-only addresses are rejected; a virtual office is tolerated if the provider certifies mail acceptance, offers physical inspection access and enables the DIAN/Chamber to conduct on-site checks; residential or shared-workspace addresses with documented access rights are the standard compliant structure for hyper-casual publishers.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low statistical risk (<10% annual probability) for a low-risk ISIC 5820 software publisher with no commercial-establishment registration requirement; probability rises to a moderate 15-25% if the registered address is a dense virtual-office cluster or if the SARLAFT/AML profile shows adverse hits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada); Código de Comercio, Decreto 410 de 1971, Articles 110 and 354-366; Decreto 1074 de 2015 (single regulatory decree for commercial registries and Chambers of Commerce).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio with territorial competence over the registered office, operating through the Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation instrument) of a Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada; optional notarization as Escritura Pública before a Colombian Notary where contributions include real property.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; the bylaws freely set authorized, subscribed, and paid-up capital. Subscribed shares must be fully paid within two (2) years from subscription; capital contributions are deposited in a Colombian financial institution (no escrow required, except bank clearing holds for cheques or foreign remittances).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 001 OF [CITY]. The sole shareholder and appointed directors, acting under Law 1258 of 2008 and the company's bylaws, unanimously resolve as follows. (1) Ratify the subscription of authorized share capital, acknowledging receipt of the paid-up portion in cash and non-cash contributions. (2) Adopt the registered office stated in the incorporation instrument, within the territorial jurisdiction of the Chamber of Commerce. (3) Appoint [Name] as Legal Representative and General Manager, with full and sufficient powers; appoint [Name] as Statutory Auditor when legally required. (4) Authorize the Legal Representative to register the company with the Cámara de Comercio, DIAN, municipal treasury, and social security entities, and to open corporate payment accounts for AdMob and AppLovin. (5) Ratify all initial administrative acts. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Verification (Certificado de Homonimia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio competente for the registered office, via the Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) virtual portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File one to three proposed corporate names through the Chamber of Commerce online system to verify the absence of identical or confusingly similar registered trade names, trademarks, or existing companies. Obtain the formal name availability certificate before executing the bylaws; the certificate typically remains valid for 30 calendar days.
required_dossiers: RUES name-search application form
Identity document of each subscriber (cédula or passport)
Proposed corporate name list in descending preference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If one or all names are refused for similarity to an existing registered entity, submit alternate names immediately. A formal refusal may be challenged by filing a recurso de reposición before the same Chamber of Commerce within ten working days, followed by a recurso de apelación to the Superintendencia de Sociedades if the reconsideration is denied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Optional Notarization of the Incorporation Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Colombian Notary in the registration circuit (optional notarization) and the drafting corporate attorney.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SAS bylaws in compliance with Law 1258 of 2008, covering corporate name, domicile, corporate purpose (ISIC 5820 software publishing and mobile game monetization), authorized/subscribed/paid capital, share classes, board and management structure, audit rules, and liquidation. Execute the Documento Privado de Constitución signed by all shareholders; where contributions include real estate or where stronger evidentiary standing is desired, elevate the document to a public deed before a Colombian Notary.
required_dossiers: Draft bylaws (Documento Privado de Constitución)
Identity documents of all subscribers
Corporate name availability certificate
Foreign investor RUT preliminary registration if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notary raises objections regarding legal capacity, capital clauses, or corporate object, amend the affected provisions and re-execute the instrument. Where an executed private document contains defects, execute an aclaratory act (aclaración) or ratify the corrected document before the same notary or chamber.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Registry Registration and Issuance of Matrícula Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Registro Mercantil Office), physically or through the RUES online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed incorporation instrument together with the pre-RUT, pay the registration fee and commercial registry impost calculated on the authorized capital, and request inscription in the Mercantile Registry. Upon successful registration, the Chamber issues the Certificado de Cámara de Comercio evidencing legal existence, corporate representation, and the company's registered office.
required_dossiers: Executed Documento Privado de Constitución
Preliminary RUT slip (pre-RUT) obtained from DIAN
Receipt of payment of registry fees and taxes
Certificate of name availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues an observation (observación), file a corrective amendment within ten working days. A refusal may be contested through recurso de reposición before the Chamber and recurso de apelación before the Superintendencia de Sociedades; judicial protection via a writ of nullity remains available thereafter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Registration (RUT) and NIT Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) through the MUISCA electronic portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) online, selecting the income tax regime, the applicable economic activities codes (including software publishing and electronic advertisement services), and the invoicing system parameters. Obtain the NIT (Tax Identification Number) and confirm electronic invoicing obligations, tax residency, and mechanisms for receiving inbound AdMob and AppLovin payment remittances.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Cámara de Comercio (mercantile registration certificate)
Identity document of the legal representative
Lease deed or proof of registered office address
Executed bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects or flags the registration due to an activity-code mismatch, submit a corrective RUT filing that realigns the economic activities with ISIC 5820. Any assessed inconsistency in the tax identification data must be resolved before the company generates any electronic invoice or receives payment from advertising platforms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating Registration and Fire Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal or District Treasury (Secretaría de Hacienda) for Industria y Comercio registration; Cuerpo de Bomberos for the fire safety technical certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the commercial establishment under the municipal Impuesto de Industria y Comercio (ICA) system and obtain the corresponding operating certificate for the physical software development office. Apply to the local fire department for the concepto técnico de bomberos evaluating fire extinguishers, alarms, evacuation routes, and emergency signage; coordinate the structural load inspection under NSR-10 to certify safe occupancy for the workforce and IT equipment.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Cámara de Comercio
RUT and NIT number
Lease contract for the office premises
Building occupancy certificate or structural load evaluation report
Fire protection system documentation for the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal treasury alerts on incomplete data, rectify the ICA registration within ten working days. If the fire department issues a non-compliance certificate, install the required extinguisher units, alarms, and evacuation signage, then request a reinspection; continued refusal may be cured by submitting an updated engineering report to the local civil defense office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Secretaría de Hacienda Municipal (Industria y Comercio) and Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (consumer protection and software quality oversight); no industrial manufacturing license applies to ISIC 5820 software game publishing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro de Industria y Comercio (ICA) municipal operating registration and Matrícula Mercantil; hyper-casual mobile game publishing is exempt from any sectoral industrial manufacturing or telecom concession permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) and the local Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) for residual environmental matters.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category Non-Industrial Office Activity; no full EIA report or environmental license required for ISIC 5820 software publishing; the activity is treated as a service activity with negligible environmental footprint.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions are generated by hyper-casual game publishing; office solid waste must comply with Decree 1077 of 2015 waste management rules; any servers or IT scrap must follow Resolution 1512 of 2010 (RAEE - electrical and electronic waste) take-back obligations; noise and thermal emissions remain within the thresholds of Resolution 0627 of 2006.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos under the local fire code, covering extinguishers, emergency exits, alarm systems, and evacuation plans; structural load and occupancy inspection under NSR-10 seismic-resistant construction regulations; occupational health and workplace clearance under the Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SG-SST) registered with an ARL occupational risk insurer per Decree 1072 of 2015.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — Colombia's national tax and customs authority; official portal and transactional systems: www.dian.gov.co (MUISCA corporate portal for NIT/RUT registration, filings, and electronic invoice validation).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Standard procedure for a Colombian S.A.S. to obtain its NIT and VAT status: (1) file the certificate of incorporation with the competent Cámara de Comercio and register in the RUES (Registro Único Empresarial y Social), which automatically generates a provisional NIT; (2) immediately thereafter, update the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) through the MUISCA portal or DIAN service window, confirming the definitive NIT, corporate address, legal representative, and the tax obligations applicable (corporate income tax, VAT/IVA, withholding taxes, electronic invoicing); (3) obtain the DIAN-issued RUT certificate and activate the mandatory electronic invoicing regime; (4) for foreign entities without a Colombian establishment, apply instead for a foreign-entity NIT by appointing a fiscal representative in Colombia, submitting certified constitutional documents with apostille or legalization, and completing the MUISCA foreign-registration workflow. Completion of these steps confers legal capacity to issue invoices, claim VAT refunds, and obtain the digital certificate required for real-time e-invoicing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Colombian-resident S.A.S. is an opaque entity subject to corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre la Renta) at the 35% statutory rate for FY2025 on worldwide income; pass-through eligibility is not available for standard S.A.S. entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not operate a check-the-box or elective entity-classification regime; entity classification is determined by law. The following statutory elections are available: (i) consolidated taxation ('Régimen de Consolidación Fiscal') for economic groups domiciled in Colombia with a direct or indirect common control of at least 90%, subject to prior DIAN authorization and an irreversible minimum two-year election; (ii) election of the integrated SIMPLE regime ('Régimen Simple de Tributación', Arts. 905–922 E.T.) for eligible SMEs with prior-year gross revenues not exceeding 119,000 UVT (approximately COP 5.93 billion for FY2025), which replaces the ordinary CIT/VAT mechanics with a combined turnover-based taxation; and (iii) application of the anti-hybrid mismatch rules introduced by Law 1819/2016 (BEPS Action 2), which disallow hybrid branch and hybrid instrument benefits rather than offering elective alignment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (IVA — Impuesto sobre las Ventas), Title IV of the Colombian Tax Statute (Articles 420 et seq.), as amended by Law 1819/2016, Law 2010/2019 and Law 2277/2022, and regulated under the compilatory provisions of Decree 1625/2016.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis turnover threshold: every person performing taxable acts ('hechos generadores') in Colombia — including foreign digital service providers and e-commerce platforms with local nexus — is statutorily required to register with DIAN and charge VAT irrespective of revenue volume. For eligibility to opt into the SIMPLE regime, prior-year gross revenue must not exceed approximately COP 5.93 billion (119,000 UVT at a UVT value of COP 49,799 for FY2025).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing ('factura electrónica de venta'): all VAT-responsible taxpayers must generate XML documents in UBL 2.1 format per DIAN's technical annex, transmit them synchronously to DIAN web services (SOAP/REST APIs) through accredited billing software or technology providers, and obtain the immediate DIAN validation response ('validado'/'no validado') before legal issuance of the invoice. Validated invoices are stamped with the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) and must be reported through DIAN's electronic event system (radicación de facturas, acceptance/rejection events). The regime requires an active digital certificate issued by DIAN-authorized certification authorities and compliance with DIAN's current e-invoicing resolutions and API specifications.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated when physically shipped abroad and formally declared with DIAN customs (Art. 481 E.T.). Services — including hyper-casual mobile game publishing, digital monetization, and advertising support services supplied through foreign platforms — qualify for the export-of-services zero-rate under Articles 462-1 and 481 E.T. provided that: (i) the service recipient is non-resident; (ii) the use or economic exploitation of the service occurs exclusively outside Colombia (e.g., game users abroad and ad consumption on international platforms); (iii) the commercial invoice, contract, and platform payout records are consistent and traceable; and (iv) the resulting foreign currency is received and repatriated through an authorized Colombian foreign-exchange intermediary. AdMob and AppLovin settlement flows, when properly documented, will normally satisfy these conditions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación — DEX) filed electronically in the DIAN MUISCA customs module; for services, the equivalent export-of-services declaration or certification where applicable
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / delivery certificate (for digital services: platform payout report, proof of online delivery, and service acceptance certificate from the foreign counterpart)

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Liquidación de Divisas) issued by the Colombian-licensed foreign exchange intermediary evidencing collection and repatriation of the export proceeds within the statutory term
Commercial Invoice of the S.A.S. expressly identifying the transaction as a zero-rated export, with the destination or foreign-use information clearly stated

Signed contract or purchase order with the non-resident counterpart, supported by AdMob/AppLovin payout statements or equivalent platform records evidencing that the economic use occurred outside Colombia
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN audits zero-rating claims by cross-matching DEX submissions, transport and contractual documentation, electronic invoices, and the Banco de la República foreign-exchange settlement records. Where export status or FX repatriation is deficient, the affected VAT refunds are retroactively clawed back in full, with reassessment of the underlying VAT, statutory default interest at the monthly rate certified by the Financial Superintendency, and the inaccuracy penalty of 100% of the misapplied amount under Article 648 E.T. Continued non-repatriation may additionally trigger loss of exporter status, denial of further refund claims, and exclusion from export-facilitation regimes. Deliberate fabrication of export documentation, misuse of payment rails, or submission of fictitious FX records constitutes tax fraud under Law 1771/2016 and may result in criminal prosecution of the S.A.S. legal representative, significant custodial penalties, confiscation of the illicit benefit, and debarment from DIAN's electronic-invoicing and refund programs.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (BDBR) — Colombia's central bank, exercising exclusive authority over the foreign exchange ('régimen cambiario') under Political Constitution Article 371, Law 9 of 1991, Decree 1068 of 2015 (Single Regulatory Decree of the External Sector) and BDBR Circular Reglamentaria Externa DCIN-83. Enforcement is co-shared with DIAN (national tax and customs authority) for sanctions related to non-canalization and foreign-trade misreporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian Peso (COP) is fully convertible for current-account operations (service exports, advertising payouts, royalties, dividends, interest) under a managed-floating exchange regime. Service exports from hyper-casual mobile gaming (AdMob/AppLovin inflows) are current-account operations; conversion into COP is not mandatory (exporters may hold USD in local foreign-currency accounts), but 100% of proceeds must be 'canalizadas' (channeled) through an authorized foreign-exchange intermediary or through a BDBR-registered foreign 'Cuenta de Compensación'. Capital-account operations (foreign equity injections, capital repatriation, debt-to-equity conversions) are freely permissible but require declarative registration of the foreign investment with BDBR via the local intermediary bank; without such registration, profit/capital remittances are legally blocked. Profit remittance hurdles: none beyond (i) valid BDBR foreign-investment registration, (ii) settled corporate income tax (35%) and non-resident dividend withholding tax (10% under Law 2277 of 2022), (iii) the bank's collection of the signed exchange declaration, and (iv) presentation of audited/signed financial statements evidencing distributable earnings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory timeline: proceeds from exported services must be received in Colombia and channeled through an authorized exchange-market intermediary within six (6) months from the invoice date or the date the service is deemed exported (Decree 1068/2015, Part 17 'Régimen de Cambios Internacionales'; BDBR Circular DCIN-83). Mandatory conversion ratio: 0% — Colombia abolished forced surrender; exporters may maintain USD proceeds in local bank foreign-currency accounts or in a BDBR-registered compensation account abroad. Declarations: an individual 'Declaración de Cambio' must be signed by the company and filed through the intermediary for each operation individually equal to or exceeding USD 10,000 (or COP equivalent); smaller ad-network payouts are consolidated daily by the intermediary. Non-canalization exposes the SAS to BDBR monetary sanctions that can reach 200% of the operation value, plus DIAN enforcement and administrative closure of the bank account.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account — combined COP current account and USD foreign-currency account for AdMob/AppLovin inflows and FX conversion
Capital Escrow Account — USD-denominated staging account for the initial FDI equity injection and subsequent channeled conversion, plus operational COP account
Operational Account — COP current account with robust digital corporate FX platform and SWIFT MT103 handling
Operational Account — COP current account; suitable as secondary liquidity account
Operational/Correspondent Account — USD clearing through Scotiabank's global network for US-origin ad-network payouts
Operational Account — COP/USD accounts with LatAm cross-border clearing strengths

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low — not compliant as primary rail. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Mercury, Payoneer, PayDo, GlobalConnect) are not authorized Colombian exchange-market intermediaries and cannot issue the mandatory 'Declaración de Cambio'. Crediting an unregistered EMI account with export proceeds breaches the canalización obligation and risks BDBR fines (up to 200% of the operation) and DIAN penalties. The only compliant use of an EMI is as a 'Cuenta de Compensación' in foreign territory expressly registered with BDBR prior to receipt, a burden EMIs rarely support. Recommended structure: direct USD payout to a Bancolombia/Banco de Bogotá USD account, then conversion through the bank's FX desk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for the SAS's legal representative ('representante legal') and all authorized signatories at the bank's head office or a major regional branch for the initial KYC interview and notarized signature registry. Remote video-call notarization is accepted by Bancolombia and Banco de Bogotá on a case-by-case basis, but only if the representative is a Colombian resident with a valid Cédula. Non-resident directors/shareholders cannot open accounts remotely: they must either (i) appear physically, or (ii) execute a special power of attorney (apostilled under the Hague Convention, translated into Spanish, and registered with the Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) conferring full banking authority on a Colombian-resident attorney-in-fact. The 'Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal' issued within 30 days before onboarding must name the representative and reflect the current board and UBO structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO/shareholder(s) controlling 100% of the SAS and injecting initial capital from foreign bank accounts; the bank classes this as a source-of-funds red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled corporate extract of the foreign shareholder; ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration under Colombian AML Act 2155/2021; bank statements (last 3 months) of the remitting shareholder account; source-of-wealth letter signed by the UBO; tax residence certificate of the beneficial owner; and the BDBR foreign-investment registration acknowledgment once the injection is conducted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, small-ticket USD inflows from US/Irish ad networks (AdMob, AppLovin) flagged as possible pass-through or structured cash layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed publisher agreements with Google (AdMob) and AppLovin; monthly payout statements from both networks; app-store analytics and game title evidence; revenue-recognition accounting policy; and the company's NIT / Cámara de Comercio registration confirming active ISIC 5820 game-publishing activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound disbursements to numerous foreign freelancers, SDK vendors, and media agencies in multiple jurisdictions without commercial substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed service contracts with each payee; pro-forma invoices matched to each MT103; board minuted approval of vendor payments; KYC identification (passport/company registry) of each foreign beneficiary; and a pre-approved beneficiary list maintained with the bank's compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATCA/CRS reporting mismatch where the US biller (Google/AppLovin) or non-resident shareholders generate inconsistent tax-residency declarations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid Form W-8BEN-E certifying the SAS's Colombian tax residence and absence of US trade or business; CRS self-certification; updated UBO matrix; audited financial statements demonstrating that the SAS genuinely publishes games and receives the ad-network proceeds for its own account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) The non-resident shareholder wires the equity contribution via SWIFT MT103 to the SAS's USD account at the chosen Colombian intermediary bank, with a transparent payment description 'Aporte de capital – inversión directa' and the beneficiary NIT. (2) The bank files the BDBR exchange declaration for foreign direct investment using the prescribed DCIN-83 form and assigns the investment registration code; this code is the legal basis for future dividend and capital repatriation rights. (3) Funds are booked as contributed equity in the SAS's statutory financial statements; the bank may request the notarized board resolution approving the capital increase. (4) If the incoming amount equals or exceeds USD 10,000, the company must sign the 'Declaración de Cambio' presented by the intermediary; for amounts above COP 50,000,000 (approximately), DIAN may also require SWIFT-adjacent document support (e.g., letter of instructions). (5) Recommended optimization: split capital injection into clearly documented tranches matching the BDBR-registered amounts to avoid mismatches between the bank's declaration and the Cámara de Comercio equity registry.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers executed in USD or COP through the local bank's FX intermediary for service disbursements — game-development outsourcing, SDK licensing fees, ad-platform media top-ups (Google Ads, Meta Ads), and legal/accounting fees. Each outbound wire above USD 10,000 requires a signed 'Declaración de Cambio' and evidence of settled DIAN withholding tax (monthly Formulario 490 for payments to foreign beneficiaries). Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary and standby) are structurally available but anomalous for pure digital hyper-casual services; they are used only when the SAS enters physical merchandise distribution (e.g., offline hardware kits, console accessories). For jurisdictions where the bank's correspondent coverage is weak (e.g., small LatAm or APAC agencies), routing via Bancolombia's or Itaú's in-house global correspondent network minimizes intermediary fees. Settlement benchmarks: incoming USD to COP credit in 1–2 business days; outgoing MT103 to US/EU beneficiaries in 1–3 business days; beneficiary pre-verification is mandatory under Sarlaft AML rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/COP Deliverable Forwards — bilateral contracts with the local intermediary bank settled against the BDBR Representative Market Rate (TRM); standard minimum notional from USD 50,000; permissible for hedging USD-denominated ad-network receivables and trade payables.

USD/COP Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) — offered by local banks and international counterparties; permissible for corporates, though local market convention favors deliverable forwards for exporters.
USD/COP FX Swaps — simultaneous spot/forward combination executed with the authorized intermediary; permissible for rolling short-term liquidity between COP operating needs and USD receivables.

Currency Options (USD calls / COP puts) — permitted for purchase from banks acting as FX counterparty; registration of the derivative with the exchange market is required when notional exceeds USD 10,000.

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) — permissible only where the SAS carries bilateral or syndicated foreign-currency debt requiring matched debt-service hedging; practically unavailable at typical hyper-casual gaming banking ticket sizes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of Commercial Registration (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the company's registered domicile
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a surcharge and, after continued non-renewal, administrative cancellation of the commercial registration; the company may be barred from issuing valid merchant certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Financial Statements and Approval Minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio, or Superintendencia de Sociedades where the company is subject to its supervision
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the 31 December fiscal year-end, generally by 31 March; if approved later, deposit within one month of approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit may result in fines by the Superintendencia de Sociedades, administrative penalties, and impediments to obtaining registry certificates and financing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre la Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April of the following tax year, according to the NIT-based DIAN filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or non-filing triggers a late-filing penalty of 5% of the tax declared or assessed, monthly default interest, DIAN ex officio assessment, and coercive collection proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Exogenous Information Return and UBO Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN, including the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (UBO registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual window set by DIAN resolution, generally in August; UBO changes and shareholding transfers must be updated within 30 calendar days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update may incur DIAN fines for failure to supply information, economic sanctions, and suspension of tax certificates; continued non-compliance may lead to enforced filing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (revisor fiscal) is mandatory where, at the prior year-end, the company has more than 50 employees, gross assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV, or gross annual income exceeds 3,000 SMMLV; otherwise no independent statutory audit is required unless the bylaws or Superintendencia de Sociedades demand one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Colombia under Law 1314 of 2009 and Decreto 2420 of 2015; Group 2 IFRS for SMEs applies to most private SAS, while full IFRS applies to listed or public-interest entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Colombian SAS must maintain an accurate record of all ultimate beneficial owners and confirm this information annually with DIAN through the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales. Any transfer or variation in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be reflected in the register and reported to DIAN within 30 calendar days of the change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva, if constituted)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – USD 1,500 per year depending on the registered address, local legal representative, and registered agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 9,000 for a small-to-medium SAS subject to a Group 2 IFRS statutory audit or statutory auditor review

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
